factors.name: Variant variability / log entropy
factors.summary: The factor collects the number and heterogeneity of variants, normalized EPA sequence entropies and most eventropy measures with positive loadings (about 0.85–0.95), and the top-k variant coverage ratios, ratio_most_common_variant and variant occurrence statistics with negative loadings. High values mean traces spread over many distinct variants instead of a few dominant ones. It is the largest factor (27.8% of variance), and several trace length, activity frequency and DFG measures cross-load on it.

factors.name: Log volume / trace length
factors.summary: Activity occurrence counts, n_events, central trace length statistics, the unnormalized EPA entropies, average_edit_distance and lempel_ziv_complexity load at about 0.7–0.9, and event_density loads negatively (-0.69). With a constant number of traces, this reflects how many events a log contains, i.e. its size in events. Many of these measures cross-load on Factor 1 or Factor 3, and n_events, epa_sequence_entropy and average_edit_distance are possible Heywood cases.

factors.name: Activity alphabet size and trace length dispersion
factors.summary: The number of unique activities and the spread of distinct activities per trace load above 0.9, together with dispersion measures of trace length (geometric std, coefficient of variation, IQR, std), number_of_ties and advanced_trace_diversity. trace_len_entropy, epa_normalized_variant_entropy and density_dfg load negatively, so larger alphabets go with sparser DFGs and more unequal trace lengths. The factor mixes alphabet size with length dispersion, and trace_len_std, trace_len_max and the global block entropies cross-load on Factors 1 or 2.

factors.name: Start/end activity concentration
factors.summary: The location statistics of start and end activity frequencies load at 0.79–0.98, while the numbers of unique start and end activities and start_activities_std load negatively. Logs with few, frequent start and end activities score high, and their DFGs have more cut vertices and higher separability. The factor thus captures a single entry and exit versus many entry and exit points.

factors.name: DFG connectivity
factors.summary: The edge count, cyclomatic number, maximum node degree and connectivity coefficient of the DFG, plus number_of_successions, load moderately (0.59–0.66). The factor reflects how many distinct directly-follows relations a log has. All five measures cross-load on Factor 1 (about 0.52–0.55), and several are linearly dependent, so the factor separates only partly.

factors.name: Loops
factors.summary: All loop measures of the Repetitions group load clearly (0.60–0.88) and nothing else does. The factor captures how often and how large loops occur within traces. n_traces_with_repetition does not join it and goes to Factor 2 instead.

factors.name: Dominant start activity (weak)
factors.summary: Only start_activities_max is assigned, with a loading of 0.66. start_activities_variance (0.59) and start_activities_std (0.49) also load on it but have stronger negative loadings on Factor 4. It seems to reflect the frequency of the most common start activity, apart from the general start concentration.

factors.name: End activity frequency spread
factors.summary: The factor rests on two nearly redundant measures, end_activities_std (0.81) and end_activities_variance (0.78), with end_activities_max at 0.37. It captures how unequal the frequencies of end activities are.

factors.name: Residual trace length histogram (weak)
factors.summary: No measure is assigned to this factor. Only low-communality histogram bins load moderately (0.31–0.55), so it should not be interpreted substantively.

factors.name: Shape of activity frequency distribution
factors.summary: activities_kurtosis (0.74) and activities_skewness (0.62) define this factor, and activities_skewness also loads -0.50 on Factor 1. It reflects how heavy-tailed and skewed the activity frequencies are, apart from their level.

factors.name: Trace length histogram bins 4 and 7
factors.summary: The factor is carried by two histogram bins, trace_len_hist7 (0.87) and trace_len_hist4 (0.84). It probably reflects a property of how the histogram bins are formed in this dataset rather than a meaningful complexity dimension.

factors.name: Extreme trace length histogram bins
factors.summary: The factor is defined by the first and last histogram bins, trace_len_hist1 (0.87) and trace_len_hist10 (0.77). It reflects how much mass sits at the extremes of the trace length range, and it is a narrow, two-measure factor.

factors.name: Frequency of rare activities (weak)
factors.summary: Only activities_min is assigned, with a moderate loading of 0.53, and activities_q1 loads 0.42. The factor may relate to how frequent the rarest activities are, but it is carried by one or two measures.

factors.name: Trace length histogram shape
factors.summary: The kurtosis (0.69) and skewness (0.66) of the trace length histogram load here, and both also load about 0.5 on Factor 3. It captures the shape of the trace length distribution as binned.

factors.name: Residual factor (uninterpretable)
factors.summary: No measure is assigned, and the largest loadings are only about ±0.3. The factor explains under 1% of variance and should not be interpreted.

interpretation.overall: The data are suitable for a factor analysis: Bartlett's test is significant and the overall KMO is 0.88. Fifteen varimax-rotated factors explain 89% of the variance, but most of it lies in four broad factors. These are variant variability/entropy (27.8%), log volume and trace length (16.3%), alphabet size with trace length dispersion (13.8%) and start/end activity concentration (11.5%). Clear smaller factors cover DFG connectivity and loops. Factors 7 to 15 are weak, often carried by one or two near-redundant measures or histogram bins, and Factors 9 and 15 have no assigned measures at all. Many measures cross-load among Factors 1, 2, 3 and 5. Six trace length histogram bins remain unassigned due to low communality, and end_activities_max and cyclicity_dfg remain unassigned due to low loadings.
caveats: The correlation matrix is singular (e.g. n_edges_dfg, cyclomatic_number_dfg, number_of_successions, activities_q3, trace_len_q3), so results rely on clamped eigenvalues and pseudo-inverses.
Possible Heywood cases for n_events, epa_sequence_entropy, epa_sequence_entropy_exponential_forgetting and average_edit_distance make their loadings less reliable.
The definitions of the measures give only their group, so the interpretations rest on the measure names and group descriptions.
Fifteen factors is a large number, and many of the later factors appear to be over-extraction or artefacts of near-duplicate measures.
Many measures cross-load on Factors 1, 2, 3 and 5, so these dimensions are not cleanly separated.
The factors describe variance shared in this set of 2112 logs, with a constant number of traces, and depend on the data, the varimax rotation and the chosen factor count.
